This is illustrative math only : - Base subtotal = package base price per traveler × number of travelers . - Standard fare — multiplier 1.0× (no premium on base). Question: What is the difference between Standard and Flex package fares? Answer: Standard uses the base catalog price (1.0×) with stricter refunds (package standard: 120+ hours, partial, 25% fee). Flex costs about 12% more (1.12×) but uses package flex: cancel 72+ hours before departure for full refundability with an 8% service fee. See Terms → Travel package catalog → Package fare types for the full table and pricing example.

[2] Source: Terms — Non-refundable bookings
Example: BK-FLT-1102 (basic international promo fare) uses policy flight basic with refundability none . Promotional and basic fares are common non-refundable examples in real life; here they are simulated . [3] Source: Document Assistant — Travel package catalog & fare types (demo)
. Flex adds 12% on top of base subtotal. 3. Night add-on = ₹1,200 × max(0, nights − included nights) × travelers (included nights match the catalog bundle, usually 1 ). 4. Total = base subtotal × multiplier + night add-on. Per traveler = total ÷ travelers. Worked example — Weekend Escape ( weekend escape ), 2 travelers, 1 night: - Catalog base: ₹4,899 / person → base subtotal ₹9,798 . - Standard total: ₹9,798 (₹4,899 / person). - Flex total: ₹10,974 (₹5,487 / person) — includes ₹1,176 fare premium. When to choose which fare: - Standard — Lowest upfront demo price; acceptable if your dates are firm and you may not need a refund. - Flex — Pay more at booking for full refundability (subject to the 72-hour window and 8% service fee in the demo engine).
